prompt: A home-goods retailer's gross margin rose from 30% to 33%, but the margin on each product was unchanged. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The retailer has probably raised prices across the board.
options.feedback: Higher prices would raise each product's margin, but every product's margin was unchanged.

options.text: Supplier costs have likely fallen this year.
options.feedback: Lower costs would raise each product's margin, which was unchanged.

options.text: Cheaper, lower-margin products are probably selling better than before.
options.feedback: That would lower the overall margin, but it rose.

options.text: Sales have likely shifted toward higher-margin products.
options.feedback: Right. If no product's margin changed, the average can only rise through mix. I'd compare each category's share of sales across the two years.

explanation: The data shows the overall margin up 3 points with every product's margin unchanged. Likely cause: the mix shifted toward higher-margin products. To test it, compare each category's share of sales across the two years. If the mix didn't change, recheck how the margin is calculated.
